title: Caramelized Shallot and Thyme Finishing Butter
description: Sweet shallot and thyme are worked into unsalted butter that melts smoothly into a warm steak gravy.

ingredients.name: finely minced shallot
ingredients.note: Caramelize fully; use only the soft browned mixture.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.note: Soften just enough to mash, reserving most for the finish.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: For softening the shallot; add gradually.

ingredients.name: fresh thyme leaves
ingredients.note: Strip leaves from stems and mince very finely.

steps.title: Caramelize the shallot
steps.text: Use a quarter of {butter} to soften {shallot} in the HexClad over medium-low heat for 12–17 minutes. Stir frequently, adding {water} a little at a time until the shallot is uniformly soft and deep gold.

steps.title: Soften the thyme
steps.text: Stir {thyme} into the shallot during the last 30 seconds. Cook until any visible water has evaporated.

steps.title: Cool the shallot paste
steps.text: Press the warm mixture through a fine sieve and scrape the soft paste into a shallow bowl. Let it cool for about 10 minutes so it will not melt the remaining butter.

steps.title: Blend the butter
steps.text: Mash the cooled shallot paste into the remaining {butter} until evenly flecked. Divide in two and refrigerate covered until needed.

steps.title: Finish at the table
steps.text: Swirl a portion into hot, thickened gravy off heat and spoon the gravy over tender beef.

notes: Make ahead: Prepare up to 3 days ahead and keep the portions covered and refrigerated. Allow about 10 minutes of cooling in addition to cooking time. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze the two portions separately for up to 1 month; the cooked shallot blends readily into hot gravy. Fridge reheat: Add the chilled butter to hot, freshly made gravy off heat and stir until melted. For leftover gravy, bring the gravy to a boil before adding butter. Freezer reheat: Thaw a portion covered in the refrigerator and use exactly as for chilled butter. For a dairy-free version, use an unsalted plant-based butter that is firm when cold. Estimated nutrition per serving of the prepared condiment (1/2 of recipe): 109 kcal, 0.4 g protein, 1.7 g total carbohydrate, 11.5 g fat, 0.3 g fiber, 3 mg sodium.

steps.title: Set up the cooking vessel
steps.text: Start the enamel Dutch oven over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes; use the lid for covered steps. Reduce heat once liquids simmer and stir across the heavy base.
